frames.narration: User 8841 opens the checkout. The page asks the SDK for the variant of experiment checkout-v2. The SDK already holds the experiment definitions from the config service, so this is a local call with no network.

The SDK hashes the layer salt with the user id and gets bucket 2310. This experiment owns buckets 0 to 4999 of the checkout layer, so the user is eligible. A second hash with the experiment's own salt gives 1900, which is below the current ramp of 2,500 (25%), so the user is in the ramp. A third hash gives 3721, below 5000, so the variant is treatment.

The page renders the new checkout. Only now, because the user really sees it, does the SDK log an exposure with a unique event id, and the same 8841 gets treatment on every device and every reload, since nothing is random.
Later the user buys something for 42 dollars. The purchase goes on the same stream. Both events are stored untouched in the raw event store, partitioned by day, and are also read by the metric jobs.

The metric job joins the purchase to the user's first exposure, drops the duplicate event id from a retry, and writes one row for 8841: converted, revenue 42.00. A nightly batch recomputes the same row from the raw store, which is what the final report uses.

Every few minutes the guardrail monitor reads the p95 latency and the error rate per arm. Treatment is at 410 ms against 405 ms for control, inside the allowed 20 ms, and errors are equal, so the experiment continues. Had a boundary been crossed, the monitor would have switched it off and paged the owner.

After the planned week, the stats engine first checks the user counts: 70,000 and 70,000 against a 50/50 plan, so there is no sample-ratio mismatch. It compares conversion: 10.0% for control and 11.5% for treatment. The planned minimum was 14,112 users per arm, so there is plenty of data.

The result is a lift of 1.5 percentage points with a 95% interval from 1.2 to 1.8, and the guardrails are fine. The owner ships it. The ramp controller moves the experiment from 25% to 50% and then 100%, and the users already in keep treatment because the ramp is a threshold on the same hash.
